edge_board.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by August 22, 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

edge_board.description: Recent military exchanges and accusations of violations have strained the fragile April 2026 US-Iran ceasefire that included Israel, particularly after July incidents involving Iranian strikes on shipping and subsequent US responses around the Strait of Hormuz. A June memorandum of understanding aimed to formalize an end to hostilities within 60 days but left key issues unresolved, including Iranian nuclear capabilities, sanctions relief, and restrictions on maritime access. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has halted direct strikes on Iran while rejecting any linkage to Lebanon operations against Hezbollah, and mediators continue pushing for de-escalation amid US diplomatic efforts. Trader sentiment on the ceasefire's continuation reflects uncertainty over compliance with these terms, upcoming negotiation deadlines, and risks of renewed missile activity or proxy escalations that could trigger market resolution.

edge_board.description: The US naval blockade of Iranian ports, first imposed in April 2026 after Islamabad talks collapsed and briefly lifted in June amid a tentative truce, was reinstated on July 14 following renewed strikes and the truce's breakdown. As of mid-August, enforcement continues under CENTCOM, with no official US announcement suspending or ending it despite earlier statements tying any lift to a signed agreement. Trader odds for an announcement by late August sit near 32-33%, reflecting Iran's August 10 posture, absence of fresh US diplomatic signals, and ongoing Strait of Hormuz tensions. Key variables include any new bilateral talks, oil export pressures, or military de-escalation steps that could prompt a formal policy reversal within resolution windows.
edge_board.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by August 15, 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

edge_board.description: The Iranian regime's demonstrated durability after the February 2026 U.S.-Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and targeted military and nuclear facilities underpins the high probability traders assign to continuity through 2026. Security forces swiftly suppressed the late-2025 to early-2026 protests with thousands of deaths, preventing defections or widespread elite fractures despite economic pressures and regional setbacks. As of August 2026, interim leadership structures under President Masoud Pezeshkian and the Supreme National Security Council continue to function, with ongoing diplomatic negotiations over issues like the Strait of Hormuz and periodic ceasefire management signaling intact central authority. Historical precedents of endurance amid sanctions, succession challenges, and conflict reinforce trader expectations that major barriers to regime change remain in place absent unforeseen escalations.
edge_board.question: Will the Iranian regime fall before 2027?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran’s current ruling regime is overthrown, collapsed, or otherwise ceases to govern by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This requires a broad consensus of reporting indicating that core structures of the Islamic Republic (e.g. the office of the Supreme Leader, the Guardian Council, IRGC control under clerical authority) have been dissolved, incapacitated, or replaced by a fundamentally different governing system or otherwise lost de facto power over a majority of the population of Iran. This could occur via revolution, civil war, military coup, or voluntary abdication, but only qualifies if the Islamic Republic no longer exercises sovereign power.

Routine political events such as elections, reforms, or leadership succession do not qualify. Internal coups or power shifts that preserve the Islamic Republic’s core structures also do not qualify. Only a clear break in continuity—such as a new provisional government, revolutionary council, or constitution replacing the Islamic Republic will qualify.

Partial loss of territory or challenges from rebel or exile groups will not qualify unless the Islamic Republic no longer administers the majority of the Iranian population within Iran. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

edge_board.description: Recent U.S. economic data and Federal Reserve communications have positioned a hold at the September FOMC meeting as the leading trader consensus outcome, with a notable but secondary probability assigned to a 25 basis point hike. Persistent inflation above the 2% target, including elevated core PCE readings and supply pressures from energy and tariffs, alongside a divided July vote featuring three dissents favoring tighter policy, have kept hike odds elevated. However, the July jobs report showing unexpected payroll declines has reinforced expectations for patience, tempering earlier momentum toward action amid a still-resilient but softening labor market. Traders continue to weigh these countervailing signals ahead of the next data releases.
edge_board.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the September 2026 meeting?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

edge_board.description: Traders assign a 96.4% probability to no Chinese invasion of Taiwan by the end of 2026 largely because the remaining timeframe is short and current indicators show no mobilization consistent with an imminent amphibious campaign. U.S. intelligence assessments have concluded that Beijing lacks a fixed timeline for unification by force and faces internal People's Liberation Army leadership challenges that complicate large-scale operations. Both sides continue gray-zone military exercises, including Taiwan's recent Han Kuang drills emphasizing resilience and coastal defense, alongside periodic Chinese blockade simulations, yet these remain below the threshold of open conflict. Deterrence from U.S. and allied posture, combined with high economic and military costs, reinforces the market consensus. Late-breaking developments such as an acute diplomatic crisis or miscalculation could still shift odds before year-end.
edge_board.question: Will China invade Taiwan by end of 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of the Republic of China (Taiwan) by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Territory under the administration of the Republic of China including any inhabited islands will qualify, however uninhabited islands will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be will be official confirmation by China, Taiwan, the United Nations, or any permanent member of the UN Security Council, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

edge_board.description: Escalating U.S.-Iran tensions since late February 2026 have kept commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz well below pre-crisis norms of roughly 100 vessels daily, with volumes averaging under 30 ships amid selective closures, vessel seizures, and elevated war-risk insurance premiums. This chokepoint handles about 20% of global oil and LNG flows, so sustained restrictions have tightened energy supply, supported higher Brent crude benchmarks, and amplified tanker rate volatility. Recent diplomatic pauses and partial reopenings in June produced only modest recovery before renewed attacks reset flows near single digits in July and early August. Traders are watching for verifiable de-escalation, formal Iranian policy reversals, or sustained daily transits exceeding 60 vessels as key resolution signals ahead of any near-term market settlements.
edge_board.question: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by August 31?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and August 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for August 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data, and do not include cases where IMF Portwatch differs from alternative sources.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

edge_board.description: Heightened regional tensions from the breakdown of the US-Iran ceasefire in July 2026, coupled with renewed military activity near the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian missile-drone responses to prior US-Israeli strikes, continue to drive trader focus on potential short-notice Israeli airspace restrictions in the Tel Aviv FIR. The airspace has reopened after repeated temporary closures earlier in 2026 but faces ongoing risks from proxy actions and cross-border incidents, prompting EASA advisories and suspended operations by many international carriers. US Embassy guidance highlights the potential for sudden disruptions, while officials emphasize security assessments that have kept civilian flights operating as of early August. Traders monitor Iranian statements, diplomatic signals, and any escalation that could trigger another closure before near-term resolution windows.
edge_board.question: Israel closes its airspace by August 15?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israel initiates a major closure of its airspace by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or complete suspension of commercial aviation across the entirety of Israeli civilian airspace or a region encompassing a majority of Israeli civilian airspace, including commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from that airspace. A qualifying closure must apply generally to all flights across Israel or a qualifying subset of Israeli airspace. Limited cancellations, delays, temporary ground stops or isolated regional closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain pre-approved flights may be permitted).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, flight suspensions, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Israel will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israeli aviation authorities; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
